data.headline: Lime by day, Waymo after parties

picks.name: Lime (monthly pass)
picks.why_you: For one month on a tight budget while hopping between cafés, fintech meetups and parties, this is the cheapest way to get almost anywhere in the city in about 20 minutes without waiting for buses.
picks.insider: Locals doing the event circuit take the monthly pass from day one, because with it each ride costs roughly $3 instead of paying full price every time.

picks.name: Muni bus / metro
picks.why_you: It's your backup for daytime trips to café coworking sessions or when you're dressed up and don't want to ride a scooter, and it's very cheap.
picks.insider: Don't buy paper tickets. Put Clipper in Apple/Google Wallet or use the MuniMobile app and grab the day pass when you'll be making several trips.

picks.name: BART
picks.why_you: Use it to get in from SFO or OAK on Monday, far cheaper than an Uber when you're bootstrapping.
picks.insider: It's great for the airport and the East Bay, but within SF it barely helps. Once you've arrived, switch to Lime or Muni.

picks.name: Waymo / Lyft / Uber
picks.why_you: After late-night parties and networking events, it's worth paying for a safe ride home.
picks.insider: Try Waymo at least once. It's the most SF thing there is, it feels safer at night, and it makes a great conversation starter with founders.

watch_out: Don't scooter home late after a party. At night, take Waymo or Lyft.
SF's hills are brutal. Plan your Lime routes so you're not pushing uphill.
Prices for Lime and the Muni pass can change, so check them in the app before paying.
Bring a jacket for night rides, since SF gets cold even in summer.

data.headline: Work cheap, meet people, land a cofounder

picks.name: Capital One Café
picks.why_you: Bootstrapped and a café person, you get open seating, solid Wi‑Fi and discounted coffee without paying for a desk, and it fits a fintech founder's world.
picks.insider: You don't need to be a customer to sit and work there, and almost nobody from out of town knows about it.

picks.name: Medium Café
picks.why_you: You work best in cafés, and this one has good internet and good coffee without the crowds, so you can do deep work on your invoicing product.
picks.insider: It's lesser-known, so you can usually find a seat. Make it your quiet 'build day' spot.

picks.name: Tandem & monthly coworkings
picks.why_you: You're here a full month and looking for a technical cofounder, so a monthly desk gives you a community to plug into, not just a chair.
picks.insider: Pick one with community events and show up to every one. Since you love meeting people, that's where cofounder intros quietly happen.

picks.name: Day-pass coworkings (~$10/day)
picks.why_you: If a monthly desk stretches your bootstrapped budget, cheap day passes let you test spaces on the days you have meetings.
picks.insider: Try a few day passes in your first week before committing to a month anywhere.

picks.name: IKEA (Market St)
picks.why_you: It's a budget-saver for long work days, with cheap food and room to sit for hours.
picks.insider: Locals use it as a stealth workspace, and it's at 945 Market St, so it's central for hopping to meetings.

picks.name: Salesforce Park
picks.why_you: It's a free, central rooftop garden in SoMa, perfect for taking calls between angel meetings.
picks.insider: The benches are laptop-friendly, so use it as your between-meetings base instead of buying another coffee.

watch_out: Core Café is the famous one and gets packed, so go early or have a backup.
Several of these spots need verifying (hours, Wi‑Fi, policies), so check before you head out on your first day.
Salesforce Park is outdoors, and SF weather changes fast, so bring a layer and a charged battery.

data.headline: Mission base, SoMa hustle, hacker-house network

picks.name: Hacker house in the Mission
picks.why_you: On a bootstrapped 1-month sprint to find a technical cofounder, living with builders is the cheapest way to turn roommates into your network, and maybe your CTO.
picks.insider: The best spots never hit listing sites, so scan Luma and X posts and ask in founder group chats this week before you land.

picks.name: Mission / Valencia
picks.why_you: Best cafés for working, the strongest Latino energy in the city, great parties, and lots of founders living nearby, which fits your vibe perfectly.
picks.insider: Stay near the Valencia corridor rather than right by the 16th & Mission BART station, which gets rough at night.

picks.name: SoMa / South Park
picks.why_you: This is where the fintech founders, pre-seed angels and most Luma events are, so it's your daytime hunting ground even if you sleep elsewhere.
picks.insider: It's buzzing by day and empty at night, so if you stay here, pick your blocks carefully and don't count on a neighborhood nightlife.

picks.name: Hayes Valley / Duboce / Lower Haight
picks.why_you: It's a solid backup if the Mission doesn't work out: central, walkable, a short ride to SoMa, and popular with early-stage founders.
picks.insider: It has a real neighborhood feel with good cafés, so you'll still get your work-from-a-café days.

picks.name: Furnished sublet (1 month)
picks.why_you: If you can't get a hacker-house spot in time for Monday, a short sublet covers exactly your stay.
picks.insider: Check Facebook groups, Craigslist sublets and Furnished Finder, and never wire a deposit before seeing the place or video-calling inside it.

watch_out: Cheap listings 'near Union Square' are often actually in the Tenderloin, so check the map before booking, especially around Market St from 5th to 8th.
Avoid the Richmond and the Sunset for this trip: they're cheaper, but 30–45 minutes from SoMa events will kill a 1-month 'meet everyone' sprint.
Nob Hill and Russian Hill are pretty and feel safe, but they're hilly and far from the event circuit, so they're not worth it for your goals.
You arrive Monday, so lock in your housing now, because last-minute options in good areas disappear fast.

data.headline: Your SF month: hackathons, Luma, Latino tech

picks.name: Entrepreneurs First (EF)
picks.why_you: Hosts a huge share of SF hackathons and founder events, and a weekend hackathon is the fastest, free way to find a technical cofounder by actually building next to them.
picks.insider: Go even if you don't plan to win, and pitch your invoicing idea to the engineers on your team as the hack project so they see how you work.

picks.name: El Gato Volador
picks.why_you: A Latino party in SF that's a great way to meet the Latino tech community, and it fits your love of parties.
picks.insider: It's posted on Luma, so follow its calendar the day you land and RSVP early.

picks.name: Luma (luma.com)
picks.why_you: About 90% of SF tech events live here, including fintech meetups and founder nights, so it's your free calendar for the whole month.
picks.insider: Follow calendars, not just individual events, and apply early because good events fill up; start this weekend before you fly.

picks.name: X / Twitter
picks.why_you: Most SF tech plans get announced on X, and it's your most direct line to pre-seed angels and fintech founders.
picks.insider: Post something like 'Landing in SF Monday for a month, building AI invoicing for LatAm SMBs, coffee's on me.' People actually reply.

picks.name: South Park Commons
picks.why_you: Its events are high-signal and full of technical people exploring what to build next, who are prime cofounder material.
picks.insider: Look for their public events on Luma rather than trying to join the community outright during a one-month stay.

picks.name: First Round Capital and Founders Inc
picks.why_you: First Round runs regular founder events and talks, and Founders Inc at Fort Mason hosts builder-heavy demo nights, so both put you in rooms with investors and builders without needing a YC intro.
picks.insider: Bring a working demo on your phone, not a deck; showing the tool turning a messy invoice into an automated one will land better than slides.

picks.name: Partiful
picks.why_you: This is where the casual parties and hangouts live, which is where your social energy turns acquaintances into allies.
picks.insider: Once you meet people at events, ask to be added to their Partiful invites; that's how you get into the house parties.

watch_out: Coffee chats are the currency here, so lean in: ask for 30 minutes, offer 'coffee's on me', and say exactly why you picked them. It fits your café workflow perfectly.
One month goes fast, so book coffee chats in week 1 for weeks 2–4 rather than waiting until you arrive.
It's cold and foggy in summer and changes block to block, so always carry a jacket, especially for night parties.
Don't fixate on YC. The other rooms on this list are often easier to get into and just as useful for finding angels.
Events fill fast and many need approval, so apply as soon as you see something good.

data.headline: Sofía's first month in SF: coffee with fintech builders, Latino founders and pre-seed angels — demo in hand, coffee's on you.

targets.who: Latino founders in SF building B2B or fintech
targets.why: Shared context on LatAm markets, warm intros to the Latino tech community, and a natural path to angels and cofounder leads. Pair this with Latino events on Luma like El Gato Volador (needs verification).

targets.who: Seed-stage fintech founder in SF (payments, invoicing, AP/AR)
targets.why: They know invoicing and compliance pain firsthand, can sanity-check your product, and often know strong fintech engineers looking for a cofounder role.

targets.why: Your #1 ask is a technical cofounder. Target engineers who've shipped payments or LLM products, ideally Spanish-speaking or LatAm-connected.

targets.who: Pre-seed angels backing fintech, AI, or LatAm founders
targets.why: First checks come from angels who already get the market. Show traction and a working demo, not a deck.

targets.who: Hackathon organizers and builders (AI/fintech weekend hackathons on Luma)
targets.why: Hackathons are the fastest, cheapest way to test-drive working with a potential cofounder. Follow Luma calendars and apply early, since good events fill up.

Looking to meet fintech founders, Latino builders, pre-seed angels, and a technical cofounder. I'll bring a demo on my phone, and coffee's on me ☕ DMs open! Also send me your fave Latino parties 💃

data.tagline: Sofía's SF month: café builds by day, Luma rooms by night, coffee's on you, demo in hand.
secrets: Coffee chats are the currency here: DM fintech founders, Latino builders and angels before you land, offer 30 minutes with coffee on you and a 2-minute phone demo, and book weeks 2–4 during week 1.

Luma holds about 90% of SF tech events. Follow whole calendars (EF, South Park Commons, El Gato Volador) and apply early, because good events fill up and many need approval. Then ask new friends to add you to their Partiful invites, which is how you get into the house parties.

Capital One Café lets anyone sit and work for free, and almost nobody from out of town knows about it (verify hours and policy first). Pair it with a Lime monthly pass (~$7/mo plus ~$3 per ride, check in the app) and you'll work and move around for very little. At night, always take Waymo or Lyft home instead of a scooter.

days.morning: Land and take BART from SFO or OAK into the city instead of an Uber. Drop your bags at your Mission/Valencia hacker house or 1-month furnished sublet.
days.afternoon: Buy the Lime monthly pass (check the price in the app) and set up Clipper in your phone wallet. Publish your 'Landing in SF today' X post and follow the EF, South Park Commons and El Gato Volador calendars on Luma.
days.evening: Settle in at a café on Valencia and send coffee-chat DMs to 5 Latino founders and 5 seed-stage fintech founders using the LinkedIn searches. Meet your hacker-house roommates.

days.morning: Work at Capital One Café: free seating, solid Wi‑Fi (verify before you go). Polish the 2-minute invoicing demo on your phone.
days.afternoon: Coffee chat #1: a Latino founder building B2B or fintech in SF. Ask for warm intros and which Latino events are worth going to.
days.evening: Go to a fintech or founder meetup in SoMa/South Park that you found on Luma. Take Waymo home for the first time; it makes a great conversation starter.

days.morning: Deep build session at Medium Café, your quiet spot for working on the product (verify Wi‑Fi and hours).
days.afternoon: Coffee chat #2: a seed-stage fintech founder (payments or AP/AR). Show the demo and ask which strong fintech engineers might be open to a cofounder role.
days.evening: Try a ~$10 day pass at a coworking space with community events, so you can compare spaces before committing to a monthly desk like Tandem.

days.morning: Work from the IKEA on Market St (945 Market St, verify), with cheap food and central for meetings. Answer DMs from angels.
days.afternoon: Coffee chat #3: a pre-seed angel backing fintech or LatAm founders, live demo and no deck. Take calls afterward from Salesforce Park.
days.evening: Go to a South Park Commons public event from Luma and talk with technical people about what they want to build next.

days.morning: Coffee chat #4: a senior engineer with fintech or ML experience, ideally Spanish-speaking. Frame it as swapping notes, not a pitch.
days.afternoon: Coffee chat #5: a hackathon organizer. Ask which upcoming EF hackathons to apply to, then submit your application.
days.evening: Go to El Gato Volador if it's on (check the Luma calendar and RSVP early) to meet the Latino tech community. Bring a jacket, and take Lyft or Waymo home.

days.morning: Join an Entrepreneurs First weekend hackathon. Pitch your invoicing idea to the engineers on your team as the hack project.
days.afternoon: Keep building with your hack team and pay attention to which engineer you work best with; that's your cofounder test drive.
days.evening: Head to a Partiful house party with people you met this week, then take a safe ride home.

days.morning: Finish the hackathon demo and invite your strongest teammate to a follow-up coffee chat in week 2.
days.afternoon: Plan week 2 at a Valencia café: commit to a monthly coworking with community events, and book coffee chats with the angels and engineers you met.
days.evening: Look for a First Round Capital event or a Founders Inc demo night at Fort Mason on Luma, apply, and post your week-1 recap on X.
